title: kv-cache: improved memory manager and adaptive eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, paging, and spillover
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management and eviction heuristics to reduce device memory fragmentation and host paging spillover; adds telemetry and feature flag for gradual rollout
description: Context: production workloads have shown increased device memory fragmentation and host paging under mixed long-short sequence traffic which caused bursty latency spikes and degraded throughput. Motivation: reduce spillover to host pages, reduce OS page-faults, and improve steady-state tail latency by making KV cache allocation, compaction and eviction aware of fragmentation, sequence-size distribution, and continuous-batching scheduling. Design summary: 1) new MemoryManager component that tracks allocation spans and hole fragmentation metadata per-shard and globally; 2) adaptive eviction score combining recency, frequency, and contiguous-span-size (to avoid freeing many small fragments); 3) background defragmenter/compactor that coalesces adjacent free spans when GPU is underutilized; 4) limited spillover buffer tier: small pinned host buffers + compressed spill bucket for cold keys to avoid heavy OS paging; 5) scheduler integration to perform compaction/eviction during low-latency-critical windows and to bias continuous-batching to reuse hot KV ranges. Implementation notes: the PR introduces runtime/kv_cache/manager.rs (MemoryManager), heuristics.rs (eviction scoring), allocator.rs (span allocator), compactor.rs (background compaction worker), and telemetry hooks in runtime/observability/metrics.rs. Feature flag runtime.config.kv_cache.adaptive_eviction controls the new logic; default is OFF but turned ON for canary hosts. The MemoryManager keeps a lightweight free-list and maintains fragmentation metrics (largest_free_span, avg_hole_size, fragmentation_ratio) and exposes these as metrics. Eviction score formula (simplified): score = alpha*recency_rank + beta*frequency_rank + gamma*(1 - contiguous_span_ratio) + delta*size_penalty. Coefficients tuned by workload profile. To limit host paging we add a spill_bucket with two tiers: pinned_host_pool (low-latency transient spill) and compressed_cold_pool (zstd-compressed tombstone entries for very cold KV segments). The compactor runs with a CPU and GPU budget and uses a cooperative preemption hook with the scheduler so it yields when latency SLO critical requests arrive. Tests and benchmarks: unit and integration tests added under runtime/kv_cache/tests for allocator correctness, compaction invariants, and eviction determinism. Microbenchmarks in benchmark-lab/kv_cache show under mixed short(<=64)/long(>=2048) seq traffic at 64 concurrent streams: median latency improved by 9-14% and P99 latency reduced by 22% across canary models; observed RMS of host page faults dropped by ~35% and overall token throughput increased by ~6% on our p4d cluster. Backwards compatibility: on-by-default flag preserves legacy behavior. Rollout: gated by feature flag and staged canary rollout across Dedicated clusters, then full rollout after 2 weeks and no regressions. Follow-ups: metric-driven autotune of alpha/beta/gamma coefficients; additional heuristic for allocating large contiguous spans for pinned attention-heavy models; observability dashboard to correlate fragmentation_ratio with SLOs. References: ENG-4521 (tracking), SUP-1284 (incident), internal doc at /docs/kv-cache-eviction-v2.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Overall approach looks good. Two concerns: 1) compressed_cold_pool memory accounting and 2) safety of coalescing while KV lookups are in-flight. Please add assertions and a race test for the latter.

Aisha Patel: Added race test (kv_cache_compact_test.rs) that exercises concurrent lookup+compaction and included a safety fence in allocator.rs; updated account logic to include compressed bytes in memory usage metric.
Ravi Kumar: Can we avoid a blocking memcpy during spill to pinned_host_pool? Consider using asynchronous transfers and preallocated pinned buffers per-thread.
Aisha Patel: Swapped the spill path to use async pinned pool and IO-friendly transfers; added a small pool-size config and a fallback to compressed_cold_pool when pinned pool exhausted.
Elena Gómez: Telemetry looks good; please add an alert for fragmentation_ratio > 0.75 on Dedicated clusters.
Aisha Patel: Added alert policy in observability-pack and a dashboard tile mapping fragmentation_ratio to P99 latency.
